The Street consensus estimate for Alphabet's GAAP EPS was $2.89 as of market creation. The market resolves \"Yes\" if reported GAAP EPS is greater than that figure in the next quarterly earnings release.\n- **Source of truth:** The resolution source is the GAAP EPS listed in the company's official earnings documents. If that figure is missing, the market resolves according to the GAAP EPS figure reported by SeekingAlpha.\n- **Deadlines and defaults:** If no such figure is published within 96 hours of the 4:00 PM ET market close on the earnings announcement day, the market resolves to \"No.\" It also resolves No if the company does not release earnings within 45 calendar days of the estimated earnings date.\n- **Restatements:** Later restatements, corrections, or revisions to the initially announced GAAP EPS do not count, except for obvious immediate mistakes such as fat-finger errors.\n- **Rounding and IFRS:** Figures are rounded to the nearest cent using standard rounding, and IFRS EPS is treated as GAAP EPS.\n\nA caveat on the GAAP-versus-adjusted distinction: one commentary piece on a later quarter noted that diluted EPS of $9.11 and net income of $112.1 billion were inflated by roughly $98 billion in other income from equity securities gains. On an adjusted basis, EPS came in at $2.85 against $2.89 expected. Because these markets use GAAP EPS, the inflated headline figure is the one that would count, which is why the adjusted number is not the one that matters for resolution.\n\nPast markets for this series have resolved both ways. consistent rules for Polymarket's \"Will Alphabet (GOOGL) beat quarterly earnings?\" markets, though most of the text comes from third-party mirror sites rather than Polymarket itself.\n\n- **Core test:** The market resolves Yes if Alphabet's GAAP EPS for the relevant quarter comes in above a consensus threshold, and No otherwise. The Street consensus estimate for Alphabet's GAAP EPS was $2.89 as of market creation. The market resolves \"Yes\" if reported GAAP EPS is greater than that figure in the next quarterly earnings release.\n- **Source of truth:** The resolution source is the GAAP EPS listed in the company's official earnings documents. If that figure is missing, the market resolves according to the GAAP EPS figure reported by SeekingAlpha.\n- **Deadlines and defaults:** If no such figure is published within 96 hours of the 4:00 PM ET market close on the earnings announcement day, the market resolves to \"No.\" It also resolves No if the company does not release earnings within 45 calendar days of the estimated earnings date.\n- **Restatements:** Later restatements, corrections, or revisions to the initially announced GAAP EPS do not count, except for obvious immediate mistakes such as fat-finger errors.\n- **Rounding and IFRS:** Figures are rounded to the nearest cent using standard rounding, and IFRS EPS is treated as GAAP EPS.\n\nA caveat on the GAAP-versus-adjusted distinction: one commentary piece on a later quarter noted that diluted EPS of $9.11 and net income of $112.1 billion were inflated by roughly $98 billion in other income from equity securities gains. On an adjusted basis, EPS came in at $2.85 against $2.89 expected. Because these markets use GAAP EPS, the inflated headline figure is the one that would count, which is why the adjusted number is not the one that matters for resolution.\n\nPast markets for this series have resolved both ways. The February 2026 market resolved Yes, and a separate Alphabet earnings market resolved No on Apr 29, 2026.\n\nI'd check the live Polymarket rules for the specific market you're trading, since thresholds and sources vary by event."],"durationSeconds":9.641807867000026,"searchCount":1},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01SNh3RR2TkSJ5b6GjtaKLk3","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}
